title: Negative gearing limited to new builds and grandfathered property
headline: Established homes contracted after 7:30pm AEST 12 May 2026 lose negative gearing from 1 July 2027. Earlier purchases and new builds keep it.
summary: For residential property acquired (by contract) at or after 7:30pm AEST on Budget night, net rental losses from the 2027-28 income year can only be used against residential rental income and residential gains. Excess losses carry forward. Properties held before the cut-off are grandfathered until sold, and new builds keep full negative gearing.

history.note: Senate passed with amendments; House agreed
Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026, Schedule 2
Amending Act No. 71 of 2026: grandfathering kept on a spouse's or co-owner's death and on relationship breakdown

bigStat.caption: 12 May 2026 cut-off: contracted after it, losses quarantined

before: Net rental losses on any residential investment property reduce tax on salary, business and other income.
after: From 2027-28, for established homes contracted on or after 7:30pm AEST 12 May 2026, net losses can only offset residential rental income and residential gains.
Unused losses carry forward to later years (cancelled on bankruptcy) and can reduce the capital gain when the property is sold.
Grandfathered properties and new builds keep the old treatment. Losses for 2026-27 are still fully deductible for everyone.
exemptions: Property you contracted to buy before 7:30pm AEST 12 May 2026, until sold. The contract date counts, not settlement.
New residential dwellings. The exact definition is still pending (see caveats).
Widely held unit trusts and complying super funds, including SMSFs.
Commercial property, shares and other assets.
From 2027-28, a surviving spouse or co-owner, or a former partner after relationship breakdown, keeps the grandfathered status.

workedExample.title: Example in the Act: Henrietta's quarantined losses
steps: 2028-29: $65,000 of deductions against $50,000 rent. $50,000 is deductible; $15,000 carries forward.
2029-30: $70,000 of deductions against $52,000 rent. Another $18,000 carries forward, total $33,000.
2030-31: $20,000 of deductions against $72,000 rent leaves $52,000 net rent, which absorbs the full $33,000.
workedExample.result: Nothing is lost, but the deductions are delayed until the property earns enough residential income.

actions.text: Keep proof of when each property contract was exchanged: grandfathering depends on the contract date, not settlement.
From 1 July 2027, keep separate income and expense records for each property and track any carried-forward losses.
Get advice before transferring property between spouses, trusts or companies, or changing joint ownership: a fresh acquisition can lose grandfathering.
Buying new? Keep the date the certificate of occupancy was first issued and your contract and settlement dates.

positions.summary: Legislated new-builds-only negative gearing from 1 July 2027 with what it calls generous grandfathering.
Will "axe Labor’s negative gearing changes". Angus Taylor: a Coalition government he leads will repeal them. No repeal date or transition rules given.
Voted for the law but want grandfathering ended, saying it leaves billions in concessions in place.
Would let every investor negatively gear up to two properties, new or established.
Broadly back limiting negative gearing for housing. Sophie Scamps has floated keeping it for one property to allow rentvesting.

caveats: What counts as a new build is not settled in law. The Act leaves it to a ministerial instrument, and none was found as at 20 November 2026. The Tax Reform No. 3 Bill would set a 24-month test; it passed the House on 29 October 2026 and is before the Senate.
There is no official guidance yet on inheritance by someone other than a spouse or co-owner, or on refinancing and renovating a grandfathered property.
